title: Reliable causal control of a core symptom by a defined circuit

concept.text: The proposed innovation is reliable control of a core psychiatric symptom through a defined human brain circuit. A reproducible procedure would identify the circuit or circuit state relevant to the symptom, then apply a targeted intervention that suppresses it without disabling collateral effects. Where ethically acceptable, blinded reversal of the intervention would bring the symptom back, providing evidence that manipulating the circuit causally controls the symptom. Psychosis, compulsion, anhedonia and dissociation are possible applications, not demonstrated extensions of the depression evidence supplied here.

Conceptual synthesis: the circuit need not occupy identical anatomical coordinates in every patient. Individualized targeting could qualify if other clinical teams could reproducibly identify the relevant circuit and obtain reliable control using a defined procedure. The innovation therefore combines circuit identification, effective manipulation and reproducibility across people; identifying a symptom-linked signal or obtaining one successful treatment response would establish only part of that capability.

significance.text: Conditional significance: reproducible, blinded control would establish a practical causal intervention for the particular symptom tested. The controlled-flight analogy captures the transition from observing a complex process to controlling it reliably; it is an interpretive analogy, not a finding endorsed by the supplied studies. Successful manipulation would demonstrate a controllable physical contribution to the symptom, without necessarily revealing its complete explanation or identifying a unique circuit that generates the underlying illness.

The direct consequence would be a basis for circuit therapeutics for the controlled symptom. The 2021 personalized depression study supplies a concrete precursor: investigators linked intracranial recording and focal stimulation to an individualized biomarker and treatment location, then used an implanted sensing and stimulation device for closed-loop therapy. Extending that approach into a dependable treatment would require reproducible targeting, independent therapeutic validation and procedures that other teams could implement safely.

Conditional downstream possibilities include using controlled interventions to test which circuit states contribute to symptoms and to improve treatment selection. These possibilities depend on the specificity and transferability of the intervention. A symptom that remains suppressed only while stimulation is active has been controlled, but that result alone does not show that the illness has ended, that its relapsing course has changed, or that other symptoms will improve.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in this record is reproducible, symptom-specific causal control with acceptable collateral effects. Personalized mapping itself already has a documented human precursor: the 2021 study used multi-day intracranial electrophysiology and focal electrical stimulation to identify a symptom-specific biomarker and a location where stimulation improved symptoms in one person with depression. Its authors explicitly left generalization to a broader population untested. The gap should therefore be framed around reliable identification and validated control across patients, rather than the complete absence of human symptom-linked mapping.

Engineering synthesis: a successful system would need to distinguish a signal associated with symptom severity from a signal that usefully guides causal intervention; identify an effective target in each eligible patient; and choose stimulation parameters that control the specified symptom without disabling changes in cognition, functioning or other psychiatric symptoms. For a closed-loop system, sensing and intervention must also remain sufficiently dependable over the intended treatment period. These are requirements implied by the proposed capability, not barriers independently quantified by the supplied studies.

Therapeutic validation is a separate barrier from observing improvement during active treatment. The September 2026 depression DBS review reported inconsistent outcomes overall and called for better establishment of efficacy versus placebo. Its peer-review responses clarify that the pooled analysis used open-label data, including open-label phases of randomized studies. Such improvements can motivate further development, but they do not by themselves resolve whether the intervention outperforms sham.

The supplied evidence does not establish the earlier assertion that DBS and magnetic stimulation are uniformly anatomically coarse, nor does it establish the absence of precise symptom control throughout psychiatry. The depression-focused evidence supports a narrower problem: generalization, reliable symptom control, tolerable collateral effects and placebo-controlled efficacy remain unestablished for the full capability described here.

current_state.text: In October 2021, Scangos and colleagues reported personalized closed-loop neuromodulation in one individual with treatment-resistant depression. After identifying a personalized symptom-specific biomarker and stimulation location through intracranial recording and focal stimulation, they implanted a chronic sensing and stimulation device and delivered biomarker-driven therapy. The retained abstract reports rapid and sustained improvement in depression and explicitly states that generalization remains to be tested. The supplied abstract and captions do not establish clinical remission; this limitation does not demonstrate that remission did not occur.

A systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis published in Nature Mental Health on September 29, 2026 reported 25 open-label and randomized depression DBS studies. The final abstract reports large within-group improvements, including standardized mean changes of 2.77, 3.15 and 3.87. The supplied review does not retain the outcome or follow-up assignments needed to interpret those three estimates separately, so they should not be assigned to particular time points or treated as probabilities of benefit. The authors described sustained antidepressant effects while calling for better establishment of efficacy versus placebo and improved clinical implementation.

The inclusion of randomized studies in the review does not make its pooled estimates randomized active-versus-sham comparisons. In the accompanying peer-review responses, the authors explain that the analysis was restricted to open-label data and used only the open-label phases of randomized trials. Earlier review materials contain counts of 24, 25 and 26 studies; the final published abstract's count of 25 is the appropriate count for this record. The response document contains redactions and revision-stage material, so it clarifies the analysis without substituting for the final full paper.

Access limits constrain further interpretation. The supplied assessment of the 2021 study rests on its PubMed abstract and captions, and the 2026 article was available through a subscription preview rather than its full text. Extracted supplementary risk-of-bias tables lacked interpretable cell ratings, and their figures were not inspected. Another supplementary PDF yielded almost no text, leaving its identity and substantive contents unconfirmed in the review despite its presence in the source index. These materials cannot support a detailed independent judgment of bias or resolve additional outcome claims.

Together, the supplied sources document a personalized single-person precursor and substantial within-group depression improvements during active DBS. They do not demonstrate reproducible, blinded control of a specified core symptom across patients. Conversely, these excerpts cannot establish that no psychiatric trial has achieved such control. No comprehensive freshness search was supplied, so the field-wide position as of November 1, 2026 remains unverified; that uncertainty does not invalidate the dated findings.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: conduct a preregistered series with a justified sample size, an operational definition of one core symptom, and prespecified thresholds for meaningful suppression, reliability and failure. The study should document who responds, who does not, and how accurately the procedure identifies an effective target. An isolated n-of-1 success would not satisfy the proposed requirement for reproducibility across patients. These are proposed criteria, motivated by the documented generalization gap, rather than established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Preregistered symptom suppression meets prespecified reliability thresholds across patients

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal test: demonstrate repeatable symptom suppression with the defined manipulation and symptom return after blinded reversal, where reversal is ethically acceptable. The protocol should specify expected response and return times, assess whether blinding remains credible, and measure collateral symptoms, cognition and functioning. A result accompanied by disabling collateral effects would fail the intended capability. Reversibility would establish a causal contribution to symptom control, not necessarily the unique disease-generating circuit.
completion_criteria.label: Repeatable suppression reverses under blinding without disabling collateral effects

completion_criteria.text: Proposed therapeutic validation: an independent trial should show that a system using the same circuit-identification procedure outperforms sham on prespecified clinically meaningful outcomes. This addresses a different question from within-person switching: whether the resulting treatment provides benefit beyond the sham condition. The September 2026 review's explicit call for stronger placebo comparisons supports the need for this distinction, but does not prescribe this particular trial design.
completion_criteria.label: Independent trial demonstrates clinically meaningful benefit over sham

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: independent teams should reproduce targeting and control, report adverse effects and failures, and define the symptom, patient population and treatment duration for which the system works. Clinical deployment would additionally require usable training, safety and implementation procedures. Finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality across patients, symptoms or disorders. Durable benefit after treatment ends would be an additional achievement rather than a prerequisite for ongoing symptom control.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce targeting and control with reported treatment boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PSY-01, Mechanism-defined diseases in place of the major syndromes, concerns disease classification. PSY-07 could supply causal circuit evidence useful to that effort, but controlling one symptom would not establish a new disease taxonomy. PSY-05, Medicines designed from a confirmed human disease mechanism, overlaps in its dependence on causal understanding, while requiring a mechanism-based medicine rather than reproducible circuit control through a stimulation system.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-02, A treatment that changes the course of schizophrenia, and PSY-03, Ending the relapsing course of severe mood disorders, concern illness trajectories. PSY-07 could overlap with either if circuit intervention produced the required durable course change. Suppression that depends on continued stimulation would not by itself establish that achievement. Their supplied titles support this distinction, but their full definitions were not provided.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-06, A clinical instrument that reads an individual's psychiatric state, concerns measurement. A symptom-linked biomarker could serve as an input to PSY-07's closed-loop control, but accurate reading alone does not establish causal manipulation. Conversely, successful control of one symptom would not demonstrate a general instrument for reading an individual's psychiatric state.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-08, Selective and durable modification of a pathological memory, and PSY-10, Reopening plasticity that can repair an established psychiatric deficit, concern specific forms of lasting change. Circuit control might help enable or investigate either, but reversible symptom suppression does not establish durable memory modification or repaired function. PSY-09, A time-limited reset of severe addiction, similarly requires a time-limited intervention with consequences beyond ongoing control; PSY-07 could contribute without satisfying that separate goal.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-04, Primary prevention that lowers incidence of a major disorder, and PSY-11, Prevention of post-traumatic stress disorder by blocking consolidation, concern preventing disorders rather than controlling an established symptom. PSY-12, A session-level amplifier that lets brief psychotherapy match a full course, concerns improving the effectiveness of psychotherapy. Circuit intervention might eventually support these goals, but a PSY-07 demonstration would not establish prevention or psychotherapy amplification.

Scope synthesis: a circuit account of dissociation would fall within PSY-07 if it developed into the same reproducible, reversible symptom-control capability. A circuit explanation alone would not qualify. Dissociation remains a conditional application here and does not require a separate concept identity.

change_log.change: Preserved PSY-07's ID, title and central capability while framing the advance around reproducibility, validated causal control and tolerable collateral effects.
change_log.reason: Personalized symptom-linked mapping already has a documented human precursor; its existence narrows the missing breakthrough without eliminating the concept.

change_log.change: Replaced the asserted 2021 remission with rapid and sustained improvement, while explicitly leaving remission unresolved.
change_log.reason: The retained abstract supports improvement; the supplied material does not establish remission or prove that it did not occur.

change_log.change: Retained the final 2026 count of 25 studies, restored the reported standardized mean changes, and distinguished open-label pooled changes from sham-controlled effects.
change_log.reason: The final abstract takes precedence over revision-stage counts, and author responses clarify that only open-label data entered the pooled analysis.

change_log.change: Removed blanket assertions about anatomical coarseness and psychiatry-wide absence of a circuit switch, replacing them with bounded evidence statements.
change_log.reason: The supplied depression-focused excerpts do not establish those broader claims or comprehensively verify the field as of November 1, 2026.

change_log.change: Separated causal control, independent therapeutic efficacy, clinical transferability and durable illness modification.
change_log.reason: These require distinct demonstrations; success at one does not automatically establish the others.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to cover measurable reliability, failures, ethical reversal, collateral effects, independent replication and practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: These additions make the intended capability testable without presenting proposed thresholds as established standards or finite tests as universal proof.

change_log.change: Integrated source-access limitations and explained relationships across the supplied concept roster.
change_log.reason: Partial access limits interpretation, while roster-based distinctions preserve separate innovations without claiming knowledge of definitions that were not supplied.

unresolved_issues: Whether the full 2021 report establishes clinical remission, and its duration, remains unresolved from the supplied abstract and captions.
The outcome measures, follow-up assignments and uncertainty intervals corresponding to the 2026 standardized mean changes of 2.77, 3.15 and 3.87 were not retained in the supplied review.
The final full-text methods and interpretable supplementary risk-of-bias assessments were unavailable to the supplied review; the nearly textless supplementary PDF cannot resolve these gaps.
No comprehensive freshness search was supplied, so whether other work had demonstrated the full capability by November 1, 2026 remains unverified.
Numerical reliability and failure thresholds, eligible populations, acceptable collateral effects and ethical conditions for symptom reversal remain to be specified for a concrete demonstration.
Relationships to the other roster entries are based on their titles; their full definitions were not supplied.

brief.title: Reliable relief of a psychiatric symptom
possible: People with a disabling psychiatric symptom could receive treatment that reliably suppresses it by changing activity in a brain circuit—a connected set of brain regions. Doctors could identify the relevant circuit in each patient and target it without disabling side effects.
why: This would give patients a treatment directed at the brain activity contributing to their symptom. It would also let researchers test which circuit states help control that symptom and improve treatment selection.

sources.showed: They built an implanted device that detected a personal brain signal and triggered electrical stimulation. Depression improved rapidly and stayed improved in one person whose depression had resisted treatment.
sources.quote: Closed-loop therapy resulted in a rapid and sustained improvement in depression.
sources.cited_for: Personalized brain signals can guide stimulation that improves depression.
sources.not_established: The study did not establish reliable symptom control across patients.

sources.showed: Their combined analysis of 25 studies found sustained depression improvement during deep brain stimulation, which delivers electrical pulses inside the brain. More frequent follow-up was associated with faster improvement.
sources.quote: Furthermore, higher follow-up frequency correlated positively with the rate of symptom improvement.
sources.cited_for: Depression improved during active stimulation, but stronger comparisons with simulated treatment remain necessary.
sources.not_established: The pooled analysis used treatment phases in which participants knew they received stimulation; it did not establish benefit over simulated treatment.

shown: Scangos and colleagues have linked a personal brain signal to an implanted treatment that produced sustained depression improvement in a single patient. This is a precursor to dependable control; whether the approach works across patients remains untested.
missing: A defined procedure still needs to identify effective targets and reliably suppress the same core symptom across patients.
Repeated suppression and symptom return after concealed reversal need demonstration without disabling effects on thinking or daily functioning.
An independent trial needs to establish meaningful benefit beyond simulated treatment.
Other clinical teams need to reproduce targeting and control and establish whom it helps and for how long.

milestones.label: Symptom suppression meets agreed reliability thresholds across patients
milestones.explanation: A study registered before it begins would have to meet preset thresholds for meaningful symptom suppression and reliability across patients. This would establish repeatability beyond an isolated success.

milestones.label: Concealed reversal brings symptoms back without disabling side effects
milestones.explanation: Where ethical, repeated suppression would have to reverse under blinding, which conceals treatment status, without disabling side effects. This would establish that manipulating the circuit controls the symptom.

milestones.label: An independent trial finds meaningful benefit over simulated treatment
milestones.explanation: An independent trial using the same targeting procedure would have to show clinically meaningful benefit over sham, a simulated treatment. This would establish therapeutic benefit beyond the comparison condition.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce control and define its limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce targeting and control while reporting failures, adverse effects, eligible patients and treatment duration. This would establish the conditions under which the treatment works.

uncertain: The reliability thresholds, eligible patients and acceptable side effects still need definition.
When is reversing treatment ethically acceptable, and can treatment status remain concealed when symptoms change?
Controlling a symptom during treatment does not establish that the illness has ended or that other symptoms will improve.

page.title: Symptom-specific circuit neuromodulation
page.definition: A procedure identifies a human brain circuit—a connected set of brain regions—and modulates it to control a specified psychiatric symptom. Independent teams reproduce symptom control in defined patient populations, with measured circuit engagement and adverse effects within prespecified limits.

goal.need: WHO estimates that 322 million people had depression worldwide in 2023. Approximately one-third of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder have treatment-resistant illness. NIMH supports developing brain stimulation devices informed by psychiatric mechanisms and using individual neural recordings to guide stimulation.

statements.quote: New devices, developed with a focus on features unique to serious mental illnesses are needed to fully explore the potential of brain stimulation treatments.

statements.body: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, SUBNETS programme
statements.quote: DARPA seeks to develop new technology to enable near real-time measurement and analysis across brain systems to drive precise neural stimulation therapies

completion.title: An independent team reproduces symptom control using the same circuit-targeting procedure.
completion.criterion: An independent team repeats the same circuit-targeting and stimulation procedure in a new patient cohort. A blinded randomized comparison reproduces objective circuit engagement and clinically meaningful improvement of a specified symptom, meeting the registered protocol's efficacy and safety criteria. Where ethically permitted, concealed withdrawal and reinstatement reproduce loss and return of symptom control. The protocol defines the symptom measure, minimum benefit, response proportion, duration, sample size and adverse-effect limits.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; a combined capability test extending published NIMH experimental-therapeutics criteria and FDA clinical-testing guidance.
completion.basis: NIMH trial notices, DARPA SUBNETS, FDA rTMS guidance and psychiatric-neurosurgery guidance were searched for a joint test of symptom specificity, reversible control, replication and safety; none was found. NIMH supplies the progression from target engagement to efficacy, while FDA supplies masking and safety guidance. Independent replication of symptom-specific control is the Atlas extension; no universal numerical threshold is asserted.

milestones.title: A human study demonstrates controlled, dose-dependent modulation of the specified brain circuit.
milestones.criterion: A human laboratory study objectively demonstrates dose-dependent circuit modulation, with a valid sham or active control, an established dose range, and safety and tolerability. NIMH requires protocol-specific numerical go/no-go criteria. Depression precursor: Scangos et al. reported 1 participant, symptom improvement in 11/13 stimulation tests, and reduced amygdala gamma power in the 2 clinically improving tests among 5 with paired neural data. The OCD and PTSD reports supply symptom-linked recordings, without establishing this full controlled dose-response test.
milestones.set_by: NIMH, PAR-25-184, R61 phase; criteria apply to neuromodulatory interventions across psychiatric symptom domains.
milestones.threshold_quote: evidence that the measure(s) of target engagement can be reliably and validly manipulated in a dose-dependent fashion

milestones.title: A patient pilot establishes an association between circuit engagement and symptom improvement.
milestones.criterion: A patient pilot reproduces circuit engagement and establishes its association with symptom or functional change, with safety and tolerability. NIMH specifies no universal effect-size or sample-size cutoff. Precursors: depression, n=1, Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale 33 to 14 after 12 days and below 10 several months later; OCD, n=1, Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale 32 to 16 at 1 year 18 weeks; PTSD, n=2, clinician-rated symptom reductions of 87.65% and 36.84% at month 12. These chronic treatment observations were uncontrolled and used whole-disorder severity scales.
milestones.set_by: NIMH, PAR-25-183, R33 target-validation stage; criteria apply across psychiatric symptom domains.
milestones.threshold_quote: strength of the association between target engagement and change in symptoms/function.

milestones.title: A powered confirmatory trial reproduces circuit engagement and symptom benefit over a justified comparator.
milestones.criterion: A fully powered controlled efficacy trial reproduces circuit engagement and its association with clinical change, and demonstrates benefit over a justified comparator. NIMH requires preliminary evidence supporting an anticipated standardized effect d=0.5; this is an entry criterion, not a required observed effect. Related evidence published on 30 March 2026: 40 adults were randomized between two TMS circuit targets; 36 were analysed, and relative depression-versus-anxiety improvement differed (p=0.0195). This tested symptom differentiation with scheduled stimulation. A matching confirmatory result was not located for the recorded closed-loop depression, OCD or PTSD approaches.
milestones.set_by: NIMH, PAR-25-179, confirmatory efficacy stage; criteria cover invasive and noninvasive interventions across psychiatric symptom domains.
milestones.threshold_quote: a fully powered, confirmatory efficacy study that is likely to show superiority of the intervention over an appropriately justified comparison condition.

not_found: No published joint completion threshold for symptom-specific circuit control, blinded reversibility, independent replication and safety was found.
No universal numerical cutoff for circuit engagement, response reliability or acceptable collateral effects was found; NIMH requires protocol-specific criteria.
No independent controlled replication meeting the combined completion test was located.
The supplied 2026 depression DBS meta-analysis could not be reopened because the publisher redirected to an inaccessible authentication page.
The full 2014 psychiatric-neurosurgery consensus could not be opened at BMJ, PMC or its Harvard repository mirror.

results.finding: One participant showed dose-dependent evoked potentials; network responses were averaged over 20 repeated pulses.
results.detail: The figure reports dose-dependent responses, but the supplied text does not establish the full controlled dose-response test, including a valid control, dose range, safety and tolerability.

results.finding: In one participant, amygdala gamma power correlated with depression severity across 16 symptom ratings.
results.detail: The participant also improved during closed-loop treatment, but this uncontrolled case does not establish reproduced circuit engagement or its association with clinical change, with safety and tolerability.
results.quote: Positive correlation between gamma power in amygdala contacts 1/2 and 3/4 within the 10-min trials and HAMD-6 score.

results.finding: Across 25 trials of DBS for treatment-resistant depression, short-term symptom improvement had a standardized mean change of 2.77; patient n was not stated.
results.detail: The meta-analysis pooled open-label and randomized trials. The reported finding does not establish measured circuit engagement or its association with symptom change in a patient pilot.
results.quote: Depressive symptoms improved across short-term (6–9 months), moderate-term (12–24 months) and long-term (>24 months) time points after DBS initiation, with standardized mean change effect sizes of 2.77, 3.15 and 3.87, respectively.

results.finding: In 37 analyzed patients with OCD, 2-mA stimulation generally decreased EEG connectivity across most frequency bands versus 1 mA.
results.detail: The sham-controlled trial measured EEG and reported good tolerability, but did not establish dose-dependent modulation of the specified circuit or an effective dose range. No protocol-specific numerical go/no-go criteria are reported, and blinding efficacy was not tested.
results.quote: When we compared both groups with each other, the 2-mA group generally decreased functional connectivity across most frequency bands (EEG connectivity results are fully described in the supplementary information).

results.finding: In 25 patients with mood, anxiety or trauma-related disorders, 15 showed reduced amygdala BOLD signal with active versus sham stimulation.
results.detail: The enrolled patient group included 10 people with PTSD, but the circuit result was not reported separately for them. The study tested one stimulation protocol, so it did not establish a dose-response range. The subsequent treatment trial was unblinded and single-arm; no serious adverse events were reported.
results.quote: In the MATRD group, 15 of 25 showed a BOLD signal reduction (60%), i.e. negative parameter estimates, for active tFUS and within-subject contrasts of active vs. sham tFUS in the left amygdala region showing a main effect for active vs. sham tFUS in voxelwise analyses.

results.finding: Depression DBS pilot: in 7 patients, a previously trained brain-signal biomarker predicted clinical recovery states with 0.72 mean accuracy.
results.detail: The new cohort reproduced an association between SCC electrophysiology and depression recovery, but the paper does not establish that the biomarker measures circuit engagement or report adverse effects and tolerability. Three of 10 participants were excluded from electrophysiology analysis due to recording shifts.
results.quote: Overall, the weekly SDC biomarker-derived depression vs stable recovery states predicted the HDRS-derived depression vs stable recovery states in the RC+S cohort with an accuracy of 0.72 ± 0.16

results.finding: In 9 patients with refractory depression, BNST theta activity correlated with depression severity (Spearman’s r = 0.42).
results.detail: Active DBS reduced BNST theta activity versus sham, and theta activity tracked HAMD scores. Recordings were made off stimulation; carryover and incomplete blinding may affect interpretation. The supplied text does not report safety or tolerability results.
results.quote:
We showed that BNST theta-band activity correlated significantly with HAMD scores (Spearman’s
r
= 0.42,
p
= 0.027)

results.finding: One patient with OCD had a 62% Y-BOCS improvement six months after DBS programming.
results.detail: Repeated acute stimulation engaged symptom-associated circuit activity and improved symptoms. Chronic DBS response was observed open-label, but the text does not report safety or tolerability outcomes or establish that circuit engagement was reproduced during chronic treatment.
results.quote:
Six months from initial programming, the participant
experienced a 62% improvement in her YBOCS score (Y-BOCS-1
13) compared to baseline (Y-BOCS-1 34) (Fig. 4C).

results.finding: OCD DBS pilot: in 24 patients, early changes in neural predictability correlated with subsequent symptom improvement.
results.detail: The study reports an association between neural changes and symptom improvement, but the supplied text does not report safety or tolerability results or establish that circuit engagement was reproduced.
results.quote: Within the first two weeks of therapy, reductions in neural predictability differentiated eventual responders from non-responders and correlated with the magnitude of subsequent symptom improvement, months before stable clinical response was achieved.

results.finding: In 18 adults with treatment-resistant depression, active BNST-NAc stimulation lowered HAMD scores by 9.4 points versus sham.
results.detail: The randomized crossover trial followed open-label optimization. The supplied text does not establish that it was fully powered or confirmatory. Circuit associations were estimated using modeled electric fields and normative connectomes, rather than patient-specific connectivity measurements.
results.quote:
As shown in
Table 2
and
Figure 2
C, the mean difference in HAMD scores between active and sham stimulation was 9.4 (SD, 7.1;
p
< 0.001; 95% CI, 5.9–13.0).

results.finding: In 50 adults randomized with PTSD symptoms, active TMS reduced total PTSD symptoms versus sham at follow-up (p=0.010).
results.detail: This was described as the first trial of this approach, not a confirmatory replication. Amygdala reactivity decreased versus sham, but the primary imaging result did not survive multiple-comparison correction. The text does not report the association between circuit and symptom changes; clinical outcomes were secondary.
results.quote: From pre-TMS to follow-up, active TMS compared to sham significantly reduced hyperarousal (group-by-time interaction, p=0.018) and total PTSD symptoms (group-by-time interaction, p=0.010).
